title: Smooth quasar-convex minimization on a ball: fresh stochastic gradients
summary: Minimize expected objective gap over a public Euclidean ball with a fixed budget of unbiased, bounded-variance gradient calls.

description_paragraphs: Solve $\min_{x\in Q} f(x)$ using stochastic gradient responses queried inside $Q$. At a fixed query budget, minimize the worst-case expected objective gap of the returned feasible point.

The public feasible set is the Euclidean ball $Q=B_2(0,D)=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\le D\}$. The unknown differentiable $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ has an $L$-Lipschitz gradient on the full space. At least one global minimizer is in $Q$, and the set $S=\arg\min_{x\in Q} f(x)$ is convex.
For all $x\in Q$, let $p_S(x)$ be the Euclidean projection onto the minimizer set. The model requires
The projection onto the hidden minimizer set defines quasar-convexity and is used in analysis. Only the projection onto the public ball is an available operation.

operations.coupling: One fresh independent draw per response. There is no sample handle or scalar function value.

description_paragraphs: Each call at $x\in Q$ returns a single full stochastic gradient $g(x;\xi)\in\mathbb R^d$. Conditional on the query and past, $\mathbb E[g(x;\xi)]=\nabla f(x)$ and $\mathbb E\|g(x;\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\le\sigma^2$.

The oracle law is fixed before interaction. Each call uses fresh independent randomness. There is no value feedback or sample handle. The learner can project onto $Q$ using its public center and radius.

Return a feasible point $\widehat x\in Q$. Any measurable feasible postprocessing is allowed, including an unqueried point, random iterate or convex combination. No function value or certificate is required.
Evaluate the unnormalized loss $f(\widehat x)-f_*\,,\qquad f_*=\min_{x\in Q} f(x)$. It is finite and nonnegative. The minimizer promise means $f_*$ also equals the full-space minimum.

accounting.free_operations: Public ball projection, internal arithmetic, and storage on available information.

description_paragraphs: Every full response costs one call, including all responses to batch queries. The cap is $N\le T$ on every run. Internal computation, storage and projection onto $Q$ are free.

components.description: One full fresh stochastic gradient response.

description_paragraphs: Private randomization and arbitrary measurable adaptive queries and postprocessing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and oracle samples.
Charge each stochastic gradient response. Public ball projection, internal arithmetic, and storage are free.

guarantees.probability_space: The algorithm's private seed and all randomness in the stated oracle or environment, after the instance and feedback law are fixed.
description_paragraphs: Choose one algorithm for the public parameters. For each fixed admissible objective and oracle law, take the expectation of the objective gap over the algorithm's private random seed and oracle noise. Then take the worst case over those instances.
The call cap $N\le T$ applies on every path, independent of the average error guarantee.

bounds.derivation: Let $x_0=0$ and $x_{t+1}=P_Q(x_t-\eta g_t)$ with $\eta=\min\{\tau/(2L),D/(\sigma\sqrt{T})\}$, using $+\infty$ for the second term at $\sigma=0$. For $p_t=P_S(x_t)$, projection nonexpansiveness and quasar-convexity give $\mathbb E_t\operatorname{dist}(x_{t+1},S)^2\le\operatorname{dist}(x_t,S)^2-2\eta\tau(f(x_t)-f_*)+\eta^2\mathbb E_t\|g_t\|^2$. Global smoothness and the global minimum promise give $\|\nabla f(x_t)\|^2\le2L(f(x_t)-f_*)$, so the coefficient of the gap after absorbing the second moment is at most $-\eta\tau$. Sum over $t=0,\dots,T-1$, use $\operatorname{dist}(0,S)\le D$, and return a uniform sampled iterate. The gap is at most $D^2/(\eta\tau T)+\eta\sigma^2/\tau$.

bounds.derivation: Use Appendix D's packing with $d_0=\lceil2\log_{16/15}(2/\tau)\rceil$, $m\ge2/\tau^2$, and the radial objectives with centers of norm at most $2D/3$. Their gradients are globally $L$-Lipschitz: the radial derivative has slope of magnitude at most $L$ and its tangential Lipschitz factor is at most $L$. The affine ambient minimizer set intersects $Q$ in a convex set. The QC inner product only uses the first $d_0$ coordinates and is unchanged by projecting onto this intersection. Set the construction's width to $\Delta=\sigma/(4L\tau\sqrt{d_0 T})$. The displayed budget guard ensures $\Delta<D/16$. Equation (19) bounds the mean KL divergence by $3/64$. Pinsker's inequality and the disjoint packing therefore give a universal positive average misidentification probability. Equation (17) then yields $\Omega(LD\Delta)$, the displayed lower bound. The guard is deliberately narrower than the theorem statement to make the width condition explicit.
